item.title: New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison
item.description:
New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison

A new React/FastAPI application is available for comparing model answers, peer rankings, and a chairman’s synthesis, inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Council concept.

🧩 How it works

The application allows each conversation to select OpenRouter or Ollama, its specific models, system prompts, and an execution mode. It supports persistent conversations, attachments, and streaming with cancellation and partial-result recovery. Execution is handled through bounded and idempotent model runs, with runtime settings controlled by administrators.

⚙️ Key details

  • Dependencies: The project uses a committed uv.lock and frontend/package-lock.json to ensure reproducible dependencies.
  • TOON statistics: Token representation comparisons are provided, but these are explicitly not provider billing.
  • Ports: The backend is published loopback-only at http://127.0.0.1:8001, while the frontend is published on port 80.
  • Proxy Limits: The frontend nginx.conf and optional nginx/nginx.conf files both set client_max_body_size to 25m. A 20 MiB image becomes approximately 26.7 MiB in base64, which can successfully upload but receive a 413 error at the proxy. To support the full API image limit, the setting must be increased to 40m and the proxy layer rebuilt.
  • Resources: The backend container has a 1 GiB total memory limit in Compose. PDF workers on Linux can each have a 1 GiB virtual-memory ceiling, with two workers per API process.
  • Databases: Compose does not provision PostgreSQL or MySQL servers. Adding PostgreSQL requires exporting base runtime dependencies with --extra database and rebuilding the image. Finance and embeddings extras similarly require explicit image packaging.
  • Environments: Python 3.10+ is declared by the project, with CI and the backend image using 3.12. Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ is required by the locked Vite release; the frontend image uses Node 22, while CI tests Node 20.
  • Configuration: In Docker, keeping a specific build-time setting empty utilizes the same-origin nginx proxy. Changing this setting for built assets requires a rebuild.

🚀 Availability

Running the application requires a running Docker engine and current Docker Compose v2. The default backend Dockerfile exports base runtime dependencies only.

#OpenRouter #Ollama #Docker #FastAPI #LLMCouncil

Source: DmitryBMsk/llm-council-plus

item.title: Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama
item.description:
Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama

A new generative‑AI project template combines FastAPI, NiceGUI and Ollama for rapid prototyping.

🔍 Overview

  • FastAPI backend and NiceGUI frontend for chat.
  • Local Ollama or cloud models through LiteLLM.
  • uv workspace tooling, tests, Docker Compose and GitHub releases.
  • Requires Make, Bash, Git and uv.

🧩 How it Works

  • Clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git.
  • Navigate into it: cd generative-ai-project-template.
  • Install dev tools: make install-dev.
  • Copy the example env: cp .env.example .env.
  • Configure INFERENCE_* and EMBEDDINGS_* in .env for your model provider.
  • Start the app: make run.
  • Open the frontend at http://localhost:8080 or the backend API docs at http://localhost:8000/docs.
  • For local Ollama: make install-ollama then make run-with-ollama.

⚙️ Key Details

  • make docker-compose – Backend, frontend and Ollama in containers; Compose 2.24+.
  • make docker-compose-cuda – Same stack with GPU access for Ollama; NVIDIA drivers required.
  • make docker-compose-rebuild – Rebuild containers after source changes.
  • make run-backend / make run-frontend – Start either application separately.
  • Python PyTorch extras are optional for model development; Ollama inference runs outside Python.
  • make install-dev installs Git hooks in a checkout; make pre-commit-install reinstalls them.
  • make test-local runs offline tests.
  • Before a PR, configure the integration services and run make check – includes live LLM/Ollama/API tests.
  • make help lists all targets.
  • make deploy-doc-local previews documentation.
  • uv provisions the Python version set by requires‑python in pyproject.toml.

🚀 Availability

  • Repository: https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.
  • Local frontend: http://localhost:8080.
  • Backend API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs.

#FastAPI #NiceGUI #Ollama #Docker #Python

Source: AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template

item.title: Koreader Now Accessible via Browser Using Docker Container
item.description:
Koreader Now Accessible via Browser Using Docker Container

A new development allows the Koreader e-book reader to run inside a Docker container and be accessed through a standard web browser. This setup is built using a base image that incorporates VNC technology.

🧩 How it works

The solution packages Koreader into a containerized environment, making it accessible at a local address without needing a dedicated e-ink device or terminal interface.

  • Container Image: The provided image is named ghcr.io/zephyros-dev/koreader.
  • Base Image: It is based on linuxserver/baseimage-selkies, which facilitates browser access via VNC.
  • Access Method: Users interact with the reader by opening http://localhost:3000 in their web browser.
  • Configuration: Koreader settings are stored in the /config/.config/koreader directory within the container.

⚙️ Key details

The project supports specific tagging conventions and integrates with automated update tools.

  • Tags:
    • latest: Represents the newest version built on the main branch.
    • Koreader.version: Indicates a specific version, such as v2023.06.1.
  • Renovate Support: Users of the Renovate bot can configure automatic tag updates by extending the github>zephyros-dev/docker-koreader repository.

🚀 Availability

Users can deploy the reader by creating a docker-compose.yaml file and executing the docker-compose up -d command to start the service.

#Koreader #Docker #VNC #WebBrowser #DevOps

Source: zephyros-dev/docker-koreader

item.title: Introducing Agentbox, a Sandboxing Tool for Running AI Agents in Docker
item.description:
Introducing Agentbox, a Sandboxing Tool for Running AI Agents in Docker

A new project called agentbox has been introduced to help developers run AI agents inside secure sandboxes. This project is currently in early-stage development, meaning users may experience breaking changes between releases.

🔍 Overview

The tool is designed to work with any Docker-compatible runtime. To run it, you need a VM and Docker installed. While setting this up can be done in a variety of ways, the provided instructions are for Colima. To install it, download the agentbox binary from GitHub Releases; the installer defaults to the ~/.local/bin directory.

🧩 How it works

When initializing, the tool simplifies the process of configuring and running agents:

  • Interactive Setup: It prompts interactively for the project name, agent, mode, and IDE when needed. It then generates the docker compose and network policy files for the sandbox.
  • Secrets Directory: It automatically creates the host secret directory at ~/.config/agent-sandbox/secrets (with mode 0700) if it is missing. On version 0.17.0 and earlier, you must create this directory yourself before starting the sandbox.
  • Read-Only Proxy: The proxy mounts the secrets directory as read-only, even if you do not have any secrets yet.
  • Configuration Auditing: To inspect your configuration after initialization, you can run agentbox policy config to output the effective network policy, or agentbox compose config for the combined docker compose stack.
  • Yolo Mode: Because you are running the agent inside a dedicated sandbox, you can even try yolo mode!

⚙️ Key details

Depending on the agent image you are using, you should follow its specific setup instructions. Additionally, developers should be aware of several extension and IDE limitations within the sandbox environment:

Tool or Plugin Compatibility Status
Copilot’s IntelliJ plugin Cannot complete auth in a devcontainer
Google Gemini No official plugin available for JetBrains
OpenCode No JetBrains extension available
Pi No IDE extensions available
Hermes No IDE extensions available

#AIAgents #Sandboxing #Docker #DeveloperTools #Security

Source: mattolson/agent-sandbox

item.title: Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI
item.description:
Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI

A community-driven project has forked the Japanese Digital Agency’s open-source Government AI “GenAI” (Genai) to enable full local operation using local Large Language Models (LLMs) with an OpenAI-compatible API. This unofficial fork addresses the original system’s dependency on cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) by replacing those dependencies with local or open-source alternatives, allowing the software to run in closed network environments such as LGWAN.

🧩 How it works

The project modifies the Digital Agency’s genai-web repository (MIT License) to function in a local environment. To facilitate merging with upstream changes, the majority of modifications are concentrated in the OpenGENAI layer (backend/ and external apps), while the genai-web UI is kept largely unmodified to preserve the original user experience. The original genai-ai-api is not included in the fork; users must obtain it separately from the Digital Agency’s repository if needed.

⚙️ Key details

The fork currently stands at version v0.13.0. Key technical and functional features include:

  • Hardware Flexibility: Compatible with macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux systems with NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA DGX Spark).
  • Security & Deployment: Production builds use docker-compose.prod.yml with TLS termination on port 443. Closed-network verification uses docker-compose.verify.yml with HTTP on port 80.
  • Storage: Uses SeaweedFS (port 8333), which is not exposed to the host in production. Artifact downloads are handled via a reverse proxy through S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT.
  • Core Capabilities: Includes structured RAG, MCP integration, OCR, skills, Web SSH, and PII detection.

📋 Version History

Version Key Developments
v0.13.0 Training, procedure document/audit, and scheduling wizard
v0.12.0 Two-week work, draw.io editing, image generation chat, and per-building model control
v0.11.0 Multi-tenancy, recommended apps, and Markdown editor HTML/PPTX export
v0.10.0 Notebook features (research/organization), Web SSH, and app display editing
v0.9.0 Third implementation wave: Markdown editor and document creation with pluggable generation APIs
v0.8.0 Second implementation wave: Online forms, procedure bundles, application reception, and MCP
v0.7.0 First implementation wave: Document reading/checking, scheduling, and Excel generation
v0.6.0 PII detection, knowledge base pages, large attachment mapreduce, and Dify error classification
v0.5.0 Production static build deployment, multi-model swapping, and SAML authentication hardening
v0.4.0 Structured RAG, knowledge MCP, Dify integration examples, and My Number checking

💡 Why it matters

The project is explicitly an unofficial fork with no relationship to or approval from the Digital Agency. While early releases focused on replacing cloud dependencies with local/OSS components, the project’s philosophy has expanded to support actual municipal usage in closed networks. This allows local governments and organizations to utilize GenAI capabilities for administrative tasks (such as document processing and scheduling) without relying on external cloud services.

#OpenSource #LocalAI #JapanGov #LLM #Docker #RAG

Source: hirokawaguchi/open-genai

item.title: GitHub Actions extension allows local workflow testing in VS Code
item.description:
GitHub Actions extension allows local workflow testing in VS Code

The GitHub Local Actions Visual Studio Code extension is now available, enabling developers to run and test GitHub Actions workflows locally without leaving their editor. This tool leverages the act tool to execute the set of actions defined in .github/workflows/ files by using Docker to pull or build necessary images and run containers for each action.

💡 Why it matters

  • Fast Feedback: Instead of committing and pushing changes to test modifications to .github/workflows/ files, developers can use act to run actions locally.
  • Local Task Runner: The extension allows GitHub Actions to replace Makefile functionality, addressing the need to avoid repeating tasks.
  • Environment Parity: The environment variables and filesystem are configured to match what GitHub provides for hosted runners.

🧩 How it works

When act is executed, it reads GitHub Actions from the .github/workflows/ directory and determines the execution path based on defined dependencies. The process involves:

  • Using the Docker API to pull or build necessary images as defined in workflow files.
  • Running containers for each action based on the prepared images.
  • Matching environment variables and filesystem configurations to GitHub’s standards.

⚙️ Key details

  • Documentation: The act user guide is available at nektosact.com.
  • Community Support: Users can ask for help in the project’s discussions section on GitHub.
  • Contributing: Developers can contribute by following the guidelines found in the CONTRIBUTING.md file.
  • Development Requirements: Building and installing the tool requires Go (version 1.26.0) and Docker. Unit tests are run via make test, while fast tests without Docker use make test-fast.

#GitHubActions #VSCode #DevOps #Docker #act

Source: nektos/act

item.title: Swarms launches production-ready Python framework for multi-agent orchestration
item.description:
Swarms launches production-ready Python framework for multi-agent orchestration

Swarms introduces an enterprise‑grade, production‑ready framework for building, deploying, and scaling high‑performance multi‑agent systems in Python.

🔍 Overview

  • Swarms is described as The Enterprise-Grade Production-Ready Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework.
  • It provides a fast, flexible, and optimized environment for multi‑agent development.

🧩 How it works

  • An Agent is the fundamental building block of a swarm: an autonomous entity powered by an LLM, tools, and memory.
  • Setting max_loops="auto" lets the agent decide when the task is complete, continuing until a stopping condition is reached. This mode is recommended for open‑ended, multi‑step tasks where the number of steps is unknown.

⚙️ Key details

  • Architectures: production‑ready harnesses for sequential, concurrent, and hierarchical setups.
  • Compatibility & integrations: seamless framework compatibility with integrations for MCP, x402, and skills.
  • Optional speedups (swarms[fast]):
    Speedup Description
    RouteHub Faster model calls via a drop‑in LLM gateway; no code changes needed.
    litellm fallback Switch back to litellm by setting SWARMS_LLM_BACKEND=litellm.
    rustworkx Rust‑based graph library for faster GraphWorkflow graphs; enable with GraphWorkflow(backend="rustworkx").

🚀 Availability

  • Official Docker image swarmscorp/swarms on Docker Hub includes Swarms and its CLI on Python 3.13 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 platforms.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides developers with ready‑to‑use tooling for complex multi‑agent workflows, reducing the engineering effort needed to manage orchestration, scaling, and performance.

#AIAgents #MultiAgentSystems #Python #Docker #LLM

Source: kyegomez/swarms

item.title: Dim0 Launches Open-Source AI Canvas with Real-Time Agent Collaboration
item.description:
Dim0 Launches Open-Source AI Canvas with Real-Time Agent Collaboration

Dim0 has released an open‑source AI canvas that integrates notes, code, mini‑apps, and an AI agent on a single infinite board, all in real time.

🔍 Overview

  • Open‑source, real‑time collaborative AI canvas.
  • Notes, mini‑apps, and agents on one infinite board.
  • Infinite canvas: thousands of nodes and nested boards, smooth at scale.
  • Real whiteboard underneath: hand‑drawn shapes, arrows, images, media, and 200,000+ icons via Iconify.
  • Rich notes: Notion‑style rich text, math, code, and sub‑pages, edited in place.
  • Mini‑apps: interactive React apps that can be opened, edited, and exported.
  • Code & documents: run code in sandboxes; drop files that the agent can search (RAG).

🧩 How it Works

  • Board‑aware agent reads the canvas and selected nodes.
  • Takes multi‑step tool actions.
  • Writes results back as editable nodes.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Bring your own model: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen, and more, switch anytime.
  • Docker is the only prerequisite.
  • Install scripts fetch the latest release from the terminal.
  • The app launches without a Gatekeeper / SmartScreen prompt (ad‑hoc signed, not yet notarized).
  • Dim0 ships a standalone desktop build (macOS · Linux · Windows) that runs fully local and offline.
  • Boards live on‑device; the agent calls providers directly.

🚀 Availability

  • Open‑source under MIT license.
  • Self‑hostable; data stays yours (no training, no telemetry).
  • Open http://localhost:3000 → create a board → type a prompt.
  • Sign in to use managed AI and sync boards across devices.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Real‑time multiplayer: live cursors, shared edits, a shared agent; conflict‑free sync, solo or fifty people deep.
  • The board holds notes, code sandboxes, mini‑apps, documents, nested boards, and presentation frames, all next to each other.
  • Your whole team can be on it at once.

#OpenSource #AICanvas #AIAgents #Collaborative #Docker

Source: vcmf/dim0

item.title: DVLAA launches local security range for LLM and agent training
item.description:
DVLAA launches local security range for LLM and agent training

DVLAA (Damn Vulnerable LLM and Agent Application) is a localized security range platform for testing, educational drills, and defense verification of large language model (LLM) and agent applications. The project centers on the OWASP LLM Top 10 and Agent Application Security Top 10 risk frameworks, covering typical scenarios such as prompt injection, sensitive information leakage, RAG poisoning, tool abuse, permission boundaries, memory contamination, output processing, and resource consumption.

🔍 Overview

The platform operates as a unified training environment that integrates theoretical vulnerability introductions, interactive answering pages, and state-machine verification. It is designed as a “theory-first” entry structure, where users first review vulnerability definitions, attack surfaces, and risk boundaries before proceeding to interactive challenges. The system builds a complete training loop: from vulnerability introduction to answering, model/state machine interaction, audit panels, flag verification, and write-ups (WP).

🧩 How it works

DVLAA uses a Flask console as its main entry point, organizing capabilities into a monolithic Flask application with lightweight sidecar containers. The system validates payloads through real model responses, tool calls, state machines, or multi-turn context progression, rather than relying on hardcoded frontend rules.

  • LLM Focus: Emphasizes risks in prompts, context, RAG, output processing, tool calls, and resource consumption.
  • Agent Focus: Emphasizes goal hijacking, tool abuse, identity/permissions, supply chain, code execution, memory contamination, multi-agent communication, cascade failures, human-machine trust, and runaway agents.
  • Question Formats: Includes chat terminals, business command workspaces, product simulation skins, and read-only material workspaces depending on the track.

⚙️ Key details

The platform includes 81 local training questions, structured as follows:

Question Type Count Description
OWASP LLM Sub-questions 24 Derived from the LLM Top 10 framework
Agent Scenarios 10 Derived from the Agent Security Top 10 framework
Comprehensive Attack/Defense 11 Integrated scenarios
AWDP Attack/Defense Contest 30 Contest-based questions
Real Contest Adaptations 6 LLM poisoning CTFs adapted from real contests

Key features include:

  • Source Code & Prompt Viewer: Users can view system prompts, runtime configurations, and core implementations on question pages; runtime random flags are replaced with placeholders.
  • Model Management Backend: Supports configuration for local models, Ollama, SiliconFlow, and OpenAI-Compatible services, with API key masking and connection testing.
  • AWDP Dual-Track Environment: Offers a default product simulation track (no official image pull required) and an option to install and start official containers (Dify, RAGFlow, Langflow, Flowise, Open WebUI, n8n) for real reproduction.
  • Bilingual & Theme Support: Top navigation allows toggling between dark/light themes and Chinese/English interfaces, with preferences saved locally in the browser.
  • Learning Resources: Provides built-in Chinese study materials, Markdown/PDF upload, online reading, and material classification management.

🚀 Availability

DVLAA is available for local execution via direct Python running or Docker image deployment to independent containers. All vulnerability environments are exposed through a single gateway port (5080). Runtime data isolation ensures that model configurations, uploaded materials, and downloaded models are stored in runtime directories or Docker data volumes. An online AI security training entry point has been integrated with Prompt Airlines, providing a five-level Chinese question guide, stable WPs, and system-internal transfer for real interaction.

#LLMSecurity #AIAgents #CTF #OWASP #Flask #Docker

Source: Tcotl/DVLAA

item.title: Speaches provides an OpenAI-compatible API for speech-to-text and text-to-speech
item.description:
Speaches provides an OpenAI-compatible API for speech-to-text and text-to-speech

Speaches is an OpenAI API-compatible server that supports streaming transcription, translation, and speech generation.

🔍 Overview

  • The project aims to be the equivalent of Ollama, but specifically for TTS/STT models.
  • It is OpenAI API compatible, meaning all tools and SDKs that work with OpenAI’s API should work with speaches.
  • Supports GPU and CPU environments.
  • Deployable via Docker Compose or Docker.
  • Highly configurable.
  • Includes a Realtime API.

🧩 How it works

  • Speech-to-Text: Powered by faster-whisper.
  • Text-to-Speech: Uses piper and Kokoro models.
  • Streaming: Transcription is sent via SSE as the audio is transcribed; users do not need to wait for the audio to fully be transcribed before receiving it.
  • Dynamic Model Loading: Users specify which model to use in the request, and it is loaded automatically. The model is unloaded after a period of inactivity.

💡 Why it matters

Speaches enables specific audio-to-text and text-to-audio workflows:

  • Generate a spoken audio summary of a body of text (text in, audio out).
  • Perform sentiment analysis on a recording (audio in, text out).
  • Support async speech-to-speech interactions with a model (audio in, audio out).

#OpenAI #SpeechRecognition #TextToSpeech #Docker #API

Source: speaches-ai/speaches

item.title: Packt Publishing Launches Workshop to Build Private, Production‑Ready AI Assistants
item.description:
Packt Publishing Launches Workshop to Build Private, Production‑Ready AI Assistants

Packt Publishing announced an intensive 4‑hour online workshop that teaches participants how to build and deploy a privacy‑focused AI assistant that runs entirely on their own infrastructure.

🔍 Overview

  • Build a production‑ready, privacy‑focused AI assistant that runs entirely on your own infrastructure.
  • The workshop is delivered online and lasts four hours.
  • No cloud APIs or external dependencies are required, giving you full control over your data.

🛠️ How it Works

  • Start with OpenClaw configuration to manage local large language models.
  • Run and manage local LLMs using Docker Model Runner.
  • Follow a complete deployment pipeline that includes security hardening and integration with messaging platforms such as WhatsApp or Telegram.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Duration: 4‑hour intensive online session.
  • Requirements: Docker installed on your laptop; minimum 16 GB RAM recommended for smooth local inference.
  • Outcome: A fully functional local AI assistant running on your machine.

🚀 What You’ll Get

  • A working assistant running locally, configured with OpenClaw and Docker.
  • Integration with your choice of messaging platform.
  • Understanding of security and privacy implications.
  • A reusable architecture you can adapt for future AI projects.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Most AI assistants today rely on external APIs, creating concerns around privacy, cost, and data control.
  • This workshop teaches a different approach: building a private AI assistant that runs entirely on your local machine, giving you full ownership of infrastructure and data.

#AIassistant #PrivacyAI #OpenClaw #Docker #AIWorkshop

Source: Build, Run and Deploy AI Agents with OpenClaw & Docker Model Runner

item.title: CapRover Scalable PaaS for Application and Database Deployment
item.description:
CapRover Scalable PaaS for Application and Database Deployment

CapRover is a scalable Platform as a Service (PaaS) designed as an easy-to-use app/database deployment and web server manager that automates Docker and nginx.

🔍 Overview

CapRover provides a platform for deploying applications and databases without requiring Docker or nginx knowledge. It is designed for developers who prefer writing code over managing server configurations and those seeking to reduce costs compared to services like Heroku or Microsoft Azure.

🧩 How it works

CapRover utilizes several technologies under its interface to maintain robustness and speed:

Component Purpose
Docker Swarm Containerization and clustering
Nginx Load-balancing (via fully customizable templates)
Let’s Encrypt Free SSL (HTTPS)
NetData Performance monitoring

⚙️ Key details

CapRover supports a wide range of applications and databases, including:

  • Languages/Frameworks: NodeJS, Python, PHP, ASP.NET, Ruby
  • Databases: MariaDB, MySQL, MongoDB, Postgres
  • CMS: WordPress

Key features include:

  • Web GUI for convenience and a CLI for automation and scripting.
  • Dropdown-based installation for databases like MariaDB, MySQL, and MongoDB.
  • No lock-in; applications continue to work if CapRover is removed.
  • Setup requires only the ability to copy and paste instructions from the “Getting Started” documentation.

🚀 Availability

Further details and documentation are available at https://CapRover.com/.

#PaaS #Docker #WebDevelopment #Deployment #OpenSource

Source: caprover/caprover
